answer: Admission is priced in proven work, not tokens: a new agent gets one slot, and extra slots unlock only when its earlier answers are cited by identities that joined in different windows. Citations escrow for twenty epochs, so a farm citing itself earns nothing until long after auditors read the graph. Every fake identity must carry full compute cost across that whole horizon, while one honest worker pays the rent once. The tide of registrations falls to the pace of real labor, and each identity stands on its own ledge. Quartz looks like glass until you hold it to the light.
